runs.text: cipal, & cabeça em algum feito, ou obra;

lines.note: Completes principal from f209: the principal person or leader in an affair or deed. The repeated cipal at f209's foot is therefore a catchword. Here the scan ends obra; rather than obras.
Especially a bad deed: ruim qualifies the preceding feito or obra. This belongs to the honnin definition, not the next heading.
Hon no, 本の, something genuine or true, agrees with propria and verdadeira. Preserve the joined Fonno rather than imposing modern word division.
Hōnō, 奉納, respectfully presenting or paying something, glossed osame tatematsuru. Both circumflexes and the historical honorific expression are retained.
Payment goes to temples or varelas. Teras is embedded Japanese in italic; the example hōnō itasu starts with Fô- at the right.
Hōnō itasu, making the offering, completes split Fô-/nô. Idem refers to the preceding temple payment.

runs.text: Adu. P. Modo de amanhecer, ou

lines.note: Honobono describes dawn's dim arrival. Adu. and P. are italic usage labels; the reduplication is grammatical, not duplicate OCR.
Yo no honobono ake ni, at the first light of dawn. Preserve Portuguese amenhaã with its joined article; the Japanese aqe-/ni crosses rows.
Mairō, I shall go, completes the dawn example. Irei logo em amanhecendo confirms a prospective statement, not an imperative.
Honoka ni means faintly or indistinctly. Escasamente concerns limited sensory perception here, not merely scarcity of quantity.
Honoka ni miru or kiku: seeing or hearing faintly. The l marks alternative verbs; qi supplies ki without needing an extra u.
Completes escasamente, or poorly. The row is entirely Portuguese and needs no Japanese reading hypothesis.
Honogurai, dim, matches entre lusco e fusco. Preserve the OCR s allographs: their length does not affect this interpretation.
Before full daylight or full nightfall. Keep debem joined as printed; the next example starts Fo-/nogurai.
Honogurai uchi ni mairu means going or coming while it is dim. The gloss allows both directions of mairu here.

runs.text: tempo, que nem he eſcuro, nem claro de todo.

lines.note: Neither fully dark nor fully light. This qualifies the journey's time and completes its example.
Honomeki, honomeku, honomeita: shining faintly, of moon or stars. Retain the historical inflection list and this literal light sense, rather than only modern 'hint'.
Sparse, somewhat dark light. The final a in escura belongs to the italic adjective; OCR's roman a had generated a spurious kana hint.
Kusa no hara yori izzuru tsuki wa: the moon rising from a grassy plain. An-/ba plausibly gives anba, 鞍馬, saddles and horses, as the Portuguese confirms.

Faint moonlight over saddles, cited from Taiheiki by Taif. Iyeni is problematic: uyeni would give 'above', matching sobre, but the first letter is not sufficiently clear to force that correction. Retain Li. followed by to. as an explanatory label, not Japanese Di.

runs.text: to. Alũa que ſahia por entre as eruas eſcaſa-

lines.note: The moon was emerging among grasses. Read sahia rather than sabia: the scan and context support sair, not saber. Alũa stays joined as printed.

runs.text: mente ſe via, ou reluzia ſobre as ſellas dos

lines.note: The light was scarcely visible or shone upon saddles. Sellas has two visible l stems, repairing the shortened OCR selas.
Dos cavalos completes 'the horses' saddles'. This supports anba in the quotation without independently settling iyeni/uyeni.

runs.text: Aruore aſsi chamada de que fazem

lines.note: Hōnoki, the magnolia used for scabbards. Aruore replaces Aruere; enlarged aſsi has separate long and short s, not the OCR's impossible aßsi sequence.
Wood for catanas' scabbards. The borrowed Japanese sword word is italic here and is not made roman merely from earlier pages' practice.
Honowo, 炎, a flame. The repeated Fono- continues with woga; uo is part of the historical spelling.
Honowo ga tobichiru, flames leap and scatter. Preserve the printed a- before labareda even though it divides article from noun.
Honowo moe izzuru, flames burn forth. Initial labareda completes the previous gloss, not this new example.
A flame emerges or catches fire. Algũa's tilde position is retained rather than mechanically shifted to the other vowel.
Honpō is an established medical rule or prescription. The circumflex is visible; the verb crosses deixa-/rão.

runs.text: rão alguns medicos inſignes eſcrita ſobre algũa

lines.note: A regimen recorded by distinguished physicians for an illness. Feminine escrita agrees with regra and is not an error.
Kusuri no honpō, an established medicinal rule. This is a recipe sense, distinct from the Buddhist homograph below.

runs.text: ou receita dalgũa mezinha eſcrita em liuro

lines.note: A remedy's recipe written in a book. Mezinha is historical Portuguese for medicine and is retained.
Antigo qualifies the book preserving the prescription. This short continuation is body text, not furniture.
Honpō, 本法, one's proper law or doctrine, hon no nori. Magnification confirms a circumflex rather than OCR caron; NINJAL independently lists Fonpô.
Completes doctrina and adds Buddhist label Bup. Keep the label italic here rather than importing roman style from another page.
Honpu, 本夫, one's proper husband, glossed moto no otto. Votto represents Japanese husband, not a foreign token.
Honsai honpu pairs wife and husband. Retain the visible gap in Fon ſai rather than normalizing it from the later heading.
Completes the paired spouses' definition. Historical molher is retained rather than replaced by modern mulher.
A different honpu means ordinary human understanding or disposition. This is not the preceding husband sense.
Honpu na hito ja, an ordinary sensible person. Restore the clearly printed pilcrow before this example.
Neither foolish nor out of one's senses. Preserve desasisado and its s sequence rather than modernizing the vocabulary.
Honpuku, 本腹, the principal wife, analyzed as hon no hara. Fonno replaces OCR Bonno, with both visual and Japanese support.
Honpuku no ko ja identifies a child of the principal wife. Initial pria completes propria without inventing an unseen hyphen above.
Filho legitimo confirms legitimate birth. This belongs to the preceding child example, not the recovery entry below.
Honpuku meaning recovery is glossed moto ni kaeru and cross-referenced to Fonbucu. Preserve the explicitly documented p/b variation.

runs.text: Linha judiciaria, ou ponto dos que cõ-

lines.note: Honke here is an astrological natal line or point, not a main household. Read Linha judiciaria rather than Linhajudiuaria; the following column completes the astrology explanation.

runs.text: ſiderão os aſtrologos em que hum naceo pera

lines.note: Astrologers consider the natal point. This continues con-/siderão across columns and is not a new headword.

runs.text: por ahi julgarem o ſucceſo, fortuna, inclina-

lines.note: Por ahi, by that means, judging events, fortune and inclination. The second letter in ahi is h, not OCR b.
Honke wo toru, assessing the natal figure. Dalguem is one printed word rather than the OCR's dal guem.

runs.text: Vendo eſtas linhas, ou pontos conjeiturar ſo-

lines.note: Inspecting these lines or points to conjecture about a person. Preserve historical conjeiturar rather than modernizing it.
The judgement concerns life and customs. Retain custumes and the printed punctuation rather than regularizing them by expectation.

runs.text: Primeira carta de venda que tinha

lines.note: Honken, 本券, an original sale deed held by the purchaser. Carta here means a title document, not an ordinary letter.

runs.text: oque comprou as caſas, & a dà alem do.

lines.note: The buyer passes it on with the uriken when reselling the houses. Upright V- joins riqen on the next row.

runs.text: a aquelle que as compra delle: & ſe he

lines.note: Uriken, 売券, is the sale deed handed to the next buyer. Aquelle and delle keep their historical double consonants.

runs.text: outra carta mais antigua ſe diz

lines.note: An older deed is koken, 古券. The Japanese document name is upright within the explanation.
Honki, 本紀, a record of origins, moto wo shirusu. Preserve the short s in his-/toria rather than altering an allograph from meaning alone.
An ancient history. Antigua remains as printed, despite antigo elsewhere on the page.
Honrai, 本来, from the beginning. Desdo is historical Portuguese, not an OCR mistake requiring expansion.
Até agora, up to now, completes the temporal definition. No Japanese token occurs in this continuation.
Honryō, 本領, one's holding, glossed hon no chigyō. Preserve both long-vowel marks and the guio-type palatalized spelling.
The holding comprises lands or an estate. Herdade clarifies the property sense rather than an abstract receipt.
Honsaku, 本作, a genuine work by its maker. Keep upright long s, not NINJAL's normalized short-s headword spelling.

runs.text: & affamado official, que não he contrafeita,

lines.note: By a renowned craftsman, not counterfeit. Read official with two f stems and joined contrafeita with f, correcting meaning-bearing OCR errors.
Nor imitated: arremedada completes the authenticity gloss. It is not an independent entry.
Honsai, 本妻, principal spouse, hon no tsuma. The Portuguese mo continues below as molher without an invented hyphen.
The legitimate and principal wife. Preserve the historical household distinction rather than flattening it to a generic spouse.
Honsō, 奔走, attentive hospitality. Tōzai ni honsō suru evokes bustling east and west to attend to guests.
Completes honsō suru and starts andando. Retain the circumflex in agreement with the printed heading.

runs.text: do ſolicito, & mouendoſe compreſſa: no meo

lines.note: The host moves solicitously and hurriedly. Compressa represents closely printed com pressa, not a new compound requiring literal interpretation.

runs.text: do conuite ſe diz às vezes louuando.

lines.note: A banquet guest may praise the host with the following formula. Coto joins nai below, not the OCR's mai.
Koto nai gohonsō de gozaru praises exceptional hospitality. Visible nai repairs mai and makes the Japanese formula intelligible.
The host gives us great hospitality. Senhor is the person praised, not an additional Japanese token.

runs.text: Vea propria, ou direita, ou cami-

lines.note: Honsuji, 本筋, the main or direct channel. Its watercourse sense leads into lineage and doctrinal metaphors.

runs.text: nho por onde corre agoa. ¶ Item per met.

lines.note: Water runs through the channel; per met. introduces metaphor. Agoa remains in its historical spelling.

runs.text: filho legitimo, & morgado que vem por

lines.note: A legitimate son and principal heir. Morgado supports the main-line descent sense, not merely any child.

runs.text: linha direita. ¶ Item, Arte, ou doctri-

lines.note: Linha direita makes direct descent explicit. The next item extends the idea to an art or doctrine.

runs.text: na que vem da fonte, ou de ſeu princi-

lines.note: A teaching comes from its source. Vem is one printed word, repairing the meaningless OCR gap in ve m.

runs.text: pio por dedução ſem miſtura de outras.

lines.note: Transmission without mixture of other teachings. Preserve miſtura's allograph rather than changing s solely from a language model's preference.
Hontaku, 本宅, one's main house, hon no ie. The comparison with subsidiary houses continues below.

runs.text: paração de outras que hum tem menos prin-

lines.note: Other houses are less principal. The scan and syntax support outras, not oatras.
Completes principaes. This short row is body text: the next heading follows within the column.
Hontai, 本体, true substance or essence, hon no tai. Keep Fonnotai joined as printed rather than respacing it from the analysis.
Sustancia completes the essence definition. Its missing b is historical, not grounds for modernization to substância.
Hon u, 本有, original existence, moto yori u nari. Independent v represents u and is not a numeral.

runs.text: ou tem ſer deſdo principio. Bup.

lines.note: Existing from the beginning, marked Buddhist by Bup. The label remains italic as printed here.

runs.text: Caxas, ou moedas de cobre que ſe

lines.note: Honsen, 本銭, principal capital in copper cash. Caxas means coins here, not modern caixas as boxes.

runs.text: dão, ou empreſtão ao ganho. i, Cabedal de

lines.note: Coins given or lent at interest. Initial d in dão has lost much of its ascender; the surviving mark and emprestão context support repairing OCR cão.
The principal excludes profits or interest. This confirms the financial sense of honsen.
Honseki, 本石, the principal and tallest garden stone. Xe represents the period's se sound rather than an exotic new reading.
The stone is placed in niwas, gardens. The borrowed term is italic here and should remain easy to toggle for human review.
Honset, 本説, authentic news or teaching, refers back to Fonjet. Preserve the final t and the documented voiced/unvoiced variant.

runs.text: tas. ¶ Item, Opinião certa, ou doctri-

lines.note: True news or an established opinion or doctrine. This parallels f209's Fonjet rather than calling for a new lexical interpretation.
Completes doctrina. Fonxi lower at the right is the following page's catchword, not part of this sentence.
